data.narrative:
Jimmy Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €80M to date, founded by Antoine Guyot and Mathilde Grivet. The valuation analysis draws from a nuclear energy comp universe of 11 firms: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter.

The peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. The nuclear energy sector contains only four same-sector peers, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier datapoints yields fewer than three matches in each category—falling short of the minimum threshold required for reliable triangulation. Constructing a median from a single or two-datapoint subset would introduce material bias and is therefore excluded from analysis.

Given the constraint, this valuation depends on qualitative assessment of the broader nuclear energy peer set rather than quantitative cross-checks. Key uncertainties include the early-stage nature of most nuclear technology companies, wide dispersion in capital requirements and commercialization timelines across subsectors (small modular reactors vs. advanced fission), and limited historical exit data within the segment. A credible valuation range cannot be supported by the available data without introducing methodological compromise. Further data collection on public trading multiples and private funding rounds at comparable burn rates would strengthen triangulation.
